newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Hock Hua unit stake sold for 190 mln rgt.
newsitem.headline: Hock Hua unit stake sold for 190 mln rgt.

text.p: Unlisted Malaysian firm Langkah Bahagia Sdn Bhd said on Wednesday that it is buying a 51.8 percent stake in the Sabah unit of Hock Hua Bank Bhd for 190 million ringgit.

"We have received the approval of the minister of finance and Bank Negara Malaysia to acquire 51.8 percent in Hock Hua Bank Sabah Bhd," Mohd Nasir Ali, director of Langkah Bahagia, said in a speech at a news conference.
Langkah Bahagia will pay 190 million ringgit for the purchase of the stake, he said.
"Langkah will increase the paid-up capital of Hock Hua Bank Sabah Bhd to one billion ringgit to attain the Tier-1 status," he said. He did not disclose the current paid-up capital level of the bank.
Under Malaysia's two tier banking system, a Tier-1 status requires shareholders funds of one billion ringgit by 1998.

In a statement, the seller of the stake, Hock Hua Bank Bhd, said, "The disposal will result in an extraordinary gain of approximately 177 million ringgit in the current year against a book value of 12.80 million ringgit of the shares sold."
Hock Hua said the sale will increase the net tangible asset of the company by 1.43 ringgit per share.
Mohd Nasir said the expansion of the bank to Tier-1 status would come partly through cash injection, asset injection and possible mergers and acquisitions. "It could also go public," he added.

"Upon completion of the sale and purchase of the shares, Langkah Bahagia Sdn Bhd would make a mandatory general offer... to the remaining shareholders of Hock Hua Bank Sabah to acquire the remaining shares," a statement from Langkah Bahagia said.
Malaysia British Assurance Bhd holds about 12 percent of the remaining stock.

Mohd Nasir confirmed that Malaysia's economic adviser Daim Zainuddin was an interested party in Langkah Bahagia. "Tun (Daim) is an interested party in the deal. I am a nominee for a certain percentage of his shares," he said, without elaborating.
But he said Daim would not have a say in the management of the bank. "Tun is just an investor," he said.
He said they are looking for a new chief executive for the Sabah bank.
Hock Hua Bank Sabah has 12 branches in Malaysia. The price of 190 million ringgit works out to 17.92 ringgit per share, said John Ting Sik Kang, the chief executive officer of Hock Hua Bank Bhd.
On the basis of 17.92 ringgit a share, the price-to-earnings multiple works out to about 40 times.
When asked if the value was considered high, Mohd Nasir said, "It is fair when you are buying a strategic, controlling stake. You have to pay a premium (for control)," he said.
Ting said that by selling the shares in the Sabah bank, "We multiply our assets instead of just adding them" as would have been the case if there was a merger between the two banks.
Hock Hua Bank Sabah reported a net profit of 8.597 million ringgit in 1996 against 6.136 million ringgit in 1995, Mohd Nasir said.

Questioned about the possible injection of Hock Hua Sabah into UCM Industrial Corp Bhd, of which Mohd Nasir is a director, he said that UCM was undergoing a restructuring exercise of its own "for the time being, we are not going to (bring it) under UCM". UCM has a stockbroking arm.
The Sabah bank is one of Malaysia's smallest banks.
